PullRequest.Title: request: preserve response body timeout errors
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Chromium can reject a response body read with `AbortError` even when the abort signal's reason is `TimeoutError`. The shared fetch helper treated that as user cancellation, so callers skipped their normal error UI.

Use the signal's timeout reason to preserve the existing timeout error. Actual caller cancellation and offline behavior remain unchanged. Add regressions for timeouts before headers and during body consumption.

This fixes error classification, not the underlying cause of a slow or stalled network request.

## How to test

Use a response that sends headers and an incomplete body, then waits past the request timeout. It should report a fetch timeout rather than cancellation. Explicit cancellation should still report cancellation.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/base/parts/request/test/common/requestImpl.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/request/test/common/requestService.test.ts --grep "Fetch request diagnostics|AbstractRequestService"` — 16 passing.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/base/parts/request/common/requestImpl.ts src/vs/base/parts/request/test/common/requestImpl.test.ts` — passed.
- A local HTTP probe through the compiled helper in Chromium verified four real-network header/body timeout and caller-cancellation cases — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed on the combined validation branch.

Not run: a live cloud-session reproduction of the original network stall.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fetch-backed requests that succeed, time out during headers or body consumption, or are explicitly canceled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single existing fetch and response body read remain on the request critical path. On rejection, the diff adds only constant-time inspection of the thrown error and existing abort signal before throwing; existing finally cleanup still disposes the cancellation listener.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the URL and consume or abort its response body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fetch per logical request and, after headers, one body read; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fetch, timeout signal, body read, cancellation listener, and cleanup occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network and body consumption remain on the critical path. Changed code executes only after either rejects.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward a failed local request through the remote request channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one IPC fallback per failed local browser request when a remote connection exists; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous cancellation-shaped body-timeout error entered the same catch and fallback path as the new timeout-shaped error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing remote fallback remains on the failed-request critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One O(1) classification per rejected request; existing body buffering continues to scale with response bytes exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrency remains caller-controlled. The diff adds no retries, fan-out, queue, limiter, coalescing, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser fetch caching and the existing disableCache/no-store option are unchanged; timeout and cancellation failures remain uncached and uncoalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the production diff is confined to bounded post-rejection classification and leaves all expensive boundaries and cleanup ownership unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Request sizes, timeout prevalence, and caller concurrency vary, but none is changed by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the PR changes error classification without changing boundary count, latency source, allocation scaling, concurrency, cache behavior, or resource lifetime.

Analysis.Summary: Performance review complete for every changed file. No valid performance finding or qualifying regression fix was identified.
